title: One-step simulation of a mapped configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $y$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose a Boolean tag correctly marks the boundary of the input-head position of $c$. For any input-head position $p$ on $x$ and Boolean words $a$ and $pre$, there is a tag correctly marking the boundary of the input-head position after one step of $M$ from $c$, such that one step of the constructed machine from the corresponding virtual configuration equals the virtual configuration associated with that successor of $c$, with $p$, $a$, and $pre$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $y$
the given tag correctly marks the boundary of $c$'s input-head position
$p$ is a valid input-head position on $x$
